Reference

How auto-sync to OneDrive works

The same mechanism sits behind both New secure area and Manage secure areas. The left panel is written for the people using it; the right panel holds the technical detail for administrators.

For people

What “Auto-sync” gives your team

Plain-language — no admin knowledge needed

When you switch Auto-sync on for a stage, its Documents folder is delivered straight to the computer of everyone on it — it simply appears in File Explorer under OneDrive. Nobody has to find the site, click Sync, or set anything up.

  • You add people to the areaAdd each person by name — one at a time, no groups. That list is who's “in the know” — and who gets access.
  • The folder appears on their PCAt their next sign-in, the stage's library shows up in their OneDrive folders — automatically.
  • Everyone works in normal Windows foldersOpen, edit and save like any local file. Changes sync back for the whole team.
  • It stays light on their diskFiles live in the cloud with a green tick and only download when opened — no full copy taking up space.
  • Joining or leaving just worksAdd someone later and the folder arrives on its own. Remove them and it disappears from their PC.
An area has several stages — like Qualification, Costing, Proposal, Contract. Each stage is its own folder. Most stages go to the whole team, but a sensitive stage (costing, contract) can be limited to just a few people. You only ever get the stages you're on.
People only ever receive stages they're allowed to see. Who's on a stage sets who's in the know; the security label sets how sensitive the files are and whether they can leave managed devices. Auto-sync just delivers the folder to the people on the stage — it can never widen access.
Works on company-managed Windows PCs. On a personal or home computer, the person instead gets a one-time “Add to my files” link — same folder, one click.
For administrators

Mechanism, prerequisites & build notes

Path B — silent auto-mount via OneDrive policy

Structure
One secure area = several stages, each its own SharePoint site + document library with unique permissions and its own sensitivity label & auto-sync policy. The area team is applied to every non-restricted stage; a restricted stage carries its own reduced membership — so costing/contract can be limited without touching the rest of the area. New areas start from a configurable default stages template.
Approach
Path B — admin-pushed silent auto-mount, per stage (each stage library is its own AutoMountTeamSites entry). Not a SharePoint action; driven by OneDrive sync-client policy delivered through Intune Settings Catalog or Group Policy (ADMX).
Selector — who
Auto-mount reaches only principals with Read+ on the list. MOSE grants individual users directly — no M365/security groups — so the in-the-know list stays fully auditable.
Selector — where
Intune/GPO assignment target (device/user group) is the reach. Managed Windows only (Entra/AD-joined).

Required policies (set together)

PolicyValue

Library ID string (into AutoMountTeamSites)

tenantId=<guid>&siteId=<guid>&webId=<guid>
&listId=<guid>&webUrl=https://tenant.sharepoint.com/sites/SA-2026-0188
&version=1
// captured from the library's Sync odopen:// URL,
// or assembled from Graph: GET /sites/{id}, /drives, /lists

Security label

Container (site) sensitivity label governs privacy, external-sharing & unmanaged-device access, and the library's default file label — not list membership. Access is granted by SP/Group permissions; the label classifies and adds guard-rails. File-level labels stay encrypted through sync; delivery never decrypts or widens.

MOSE build notes — reuse shared k* libs

  • One site per stage → provision N sites/libraries per area via kSite + kSPList / kSchemaToSPList; break inheritance & set unique perms with kSPListPermissions
  • People picker (team + per-stage restrict) → SharePointPeoplePicker; stages grid → kEditableTable with a kEditableTablePeopleCell Access column (not a hand-rolled grid)
  • Membership → kSPUser / kSPPeoplePicker
  • All HTTP (SP + Graph) → kSPRest.RestExecute (relative url)
  • Library-ID assembly → Graph via RestExecute
  • Label assignment → Graph assignSensitivityLabel
  • Errors → ks.kErrorMode guard + ks.kGlobalErrorHandler(e,"Class.method")

What the admin can & can't see

  • Knowable, exact: access / membership, and whether auto-sync is targeted (On/Off) for the library. This is what the UI shows — including the per-person reverse lookup (“what does this person have access to?”), which is just a membership query across areas.
  • Not knowable from the tenant: real-time, per-user confirmation that a specific library has mounted or finished on each PC — sync runs client-side, there is no such API. So no "N/M delivered" or per-person "Delivered/Pending" status is shown; that would be invented telemetry.
  • Under Files On-Demand the folder arrives as cloud placeholders — nothing downloads until a file is opened, so a "% synced" figure is meaningless by design.
  • The nearest real signals are coarse and indirect: the OneDrive sync health report (per-device app health/errors, delayed hours, needs sync reporting enabled — not per-library) and Purview audit (file-open activity). Capability to verify against current Microsoft docs.

Constraints

  • Delivers at next sync-client poll / sign-in — not instant; removes on permission loss at next poll.
  • ~300k items / library sync ceiling.
  • Unmanaged devices → no silent delivery; fall back to “Add shortcut to OneDrive”.

Exact library-ID capture click-path to be verified against current Microsoft docs before implementation.
